title: The Peril of Overdependence
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article revisits a familiar but easily forgotten trap: becoming overly dependent on a single resource, whether it's a customer, supplier, team member, or funding source. It walks through why overdependence forms in the first place — often a lack of alternatives or simple comfort — and why the real danger isn't the initial dependency but staying in it too long. The piece frames this as a periodic self-check every leader should run, since success built on concentration can mask growing risk. It closes by distinguishing healthy focus from dangerous overreliance.
points: Overdependence on a single customer, supplier, team member, or funding source is an easily forgotten trap.
Short-term success built on concentration can mask the growing risk of relying too heavily on one source.
Comfort, familiarity, and lack of alternatives are common reasons overdependence forms in the first place.
The real danger isn't the initial dependency but failing to actively work toward diversifying away from it.
Leaders are urged to periodically ask themselves what overdependence they've inadvertently created.
quotes: It’s easy to forget a trap when you haven’t stepped in it for a long time.
Anyone who has “too many eggs in one basket” is at risk for a potential calamity.

The danger of becoming overdependent on any one thing (a small set of customers, a critical supplier, a highly skilled team member, a single source of finance) is easy to ignore because of the success leaders enjoy short term due to that concentration.
Finding yourself depending on a single source is not the main problem. As bad as that is, the real issue is staying in that position.
But when it comes to an overreliance on a single resource, concentration is the enemy.
